alignments.note: Waw rendered *And* under rule 14.
Explicit subject demonstrative takes only its own word; the copula goes to the predicate under rule 20.

Construct noun is the predicate of the verbless clause, so it carries the construction-supplied *is* under rule 20, with a supplied *the* under rule 29 since the rectum's own article takes the second written *the*.
The ASV renders the rectum arthrously, so under rule 29 nothing is fronted and this article takes the *the* standing before its own word.
Rectum takes the relational *of* under rule 19; discontinuous around its own article under rule 25.
Infinitive absolute used as the clause's finite verb; it takes the auxiliary and lexical verb under rule 17. Rule 56 does not reach it because no cognate finite verb stands beside it.
כֹּל rendered *every*.

One English word for the fixed pair בַּעַל מַשֵּׁה under rule 30, headed on the governing construct by rule 23. The competing reading gives *creditor* to בַּעַל alone and marks מַשֵּׁה unrepresented; the fusion is preferred because *creditor* carries the loan as well as the ownership.
*creditor* does not carry the idiom's *hand*, so rule 30 forbids absorbing it; the ASV writes nothing for it.
No possessive is written anywhere in *every creditor*.

Headless relative: under rule 46's first rider a written relative takes the supplied antecedent along with the relative word. Head on *which*, which directly realizes the relative lexeme; heading on *that* is the competing reading.
Finite verb with subject pronoun and auxiliary, rule 17.
Preposition rendered *unto*.
Noun.
Suffix rendered by the possessive, rule 18.
Negative.
Verb with subject pronoun and auxiliary, discontinuous around the negative under rule 25.
Rule 16's first family: the English verb reaches its object through *of* (*exact of*), and no other morpheme licenses that word.
Supplied object pronoun: the Hebrew object is רֵעֵהוּ, and this *it* answers to no morpheme, so rule 44 leaves it added.
Noun.
Suffix.
Waw rendered *and*.
The ASV writes no second *of* for this marker; rule 16's default applies.
Noun.
Suffix.
כִּי rendered *because*.
Verb recast as an English passive; the auxiliaries join it under rule 17.
Noun.

Rule 49's closing paragraph: the ASV writes no preposition of its own but an English genitive, so one word carries both the relation and the name and the pair fuses under rule 30, headed on the word carrying the lexeme.

review_notes: The בַּעַל מַשֵּׁה יָדוֹ phrase is the one genuinely contested spot: *creditor* is treated as a two-morpheme fusion with the hand phrase left unrepresented.
*that which* is headed on *which*; the same choice is taken at DEU.15.8.
